clue.text: This could help you if you are floored!

definitions.text: This could help you if you are floored!

parts.words: This could help you if you are floored!
parts.note: being floored sounds like being knocked flat, but a floor that has been covered with this soft furnishing is literally floored

explanation.definitionFit: A rug-like covering laid across a room is what gives a floor its finish.

clue.text: A type of ice-cream only two-thirds fruit

indicators.note: keeping only two-thirds of a six-letter word means its final third is cut off

parts.note: a cornet is an ice-cream in a cone

explanation.surface: A dessert menu describes an ice-cream that is only partly made of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A type of ice-cream' reads as one phrase, but A stands on its own; 'only two-thirds' keeps CORN of the cone's name, and 'fruit' is the oak's, not a flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut is its fruit, botanically speaking.

clue.text: Kitchen drudge gets work to bring in money

explanation.surface: A scullery hand takes a job to earn some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a lowly kitchen worker boils pots; it is also a hack novel or play written purely for income.

clue.text: Accepting volunteers to join man on board

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
the king is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: Volunteers are welcomed to join a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean receiving or agreeing to something offered.

clue.text: Is participating in march 'heaven'?

indicators.note: something participating in an event is placed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a parade is a procession or march
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether marching along can be heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a common synonym for the celestial realm of bliss.

clue.text: Tempter involved with Ann and megan — one retains attraction

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A seducer gets entangled with two women, one of whom stays attracted to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles TEMPTER, ANN and MEGAN together; 'with' and 'and' just join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a metal object keeps its magnetism indefinitely, drawing iron to it.

clue.text: Once again grab forty winks at the back

indicators.note: at here places one piece right up against the other, the nap coming after the back

parts.note: the rear is the back
forty winks is a short nap or rest

explanation.surface: Someone catches a quick nap at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend a suspect a second time is to take them into custody once more.

clue.text: Very bad person leading daughter to wickedness

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so the daughter's letter comes first

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family records
evil means wickedness

explanation.surface: A villain leads his daughter astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or demon is a thoroughly wicked individual.

clue.text: Result of a bad hair day when things fall apart?

definitions.text: Result of a bad hair day

explanation.surface: Messy hair seems like the moment when everything collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed hair tips come from damage; read literally the phrase describes the final parts of things breaking up.

clue.text: Country house art OK if properly displayed

indicators.note: showing these letters properly suggests they must be rearranged into their correct order

explanation.surface: Art in a country house is fine if hung well.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian nation, capital Seoul, is a country.

clue.text: Rodent in part 5 of the book series?

parts.note: VOL is the abbreviation for volume, a part of a book series
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet, so volume E is the fifth in a lettered series

explanation.surface: Does a small creature feature in the fifth instalment of a set of books?
explanation.definitionFit: A small mouse-like creature of fields and riverbanks belongs to the rodent order.

clue.text: A minion's working — it makes a real rest impossible

definitions.text: it makes a real rest impossible

indicators.note: working means in operation or being processed, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A servant is busy, so there can be no proper rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic sleeplessness prevents true repose.

clue.text: Give an account of some minstrel at Eisteddfod

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bard at a Welsh music festival tells a story.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate or tell a story is to recount events.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid in small ravine

explanation.surface: Some water sits in a little gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid measure, a quarter of a pint; also a dialect term for a narrow wooded valley with a stream.

clue.text: Repetition — one trait I developed unfortunately

indicators.note: something that developed unfortunately turned out badly, so these letters come out in a changed order

explanation.surface: Someone laments a character flaw that has grown worse with time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again and again is reiteration.

clue.text: Legal right English chaps established in Orient

indicators.note: established in means set up within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Orient is the East
chaps means men

explanation.surface: English settlers in the East secure legal entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of way or similar privilege over another's land is a legal entitlement.

clue.text: Forgetting the whereabouts of Scottish island in possession of dynasty

indicators.note: a dynasty in possession of an island holds it, so the island goes inside

parts.note: the Ming were a Chinese imperial dynasty
Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky

explanation.surface: A ruling house loses track of a Scottish island it owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing something means forgetting where it has been put.

clue.text: Little bit found in page at front of literary composition

indicators.note: at front of places the page's letter before the composition

parts.note: an article is a written piece in a journal

explanation.surface: A small fragment is spotted on the opening page of an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck or tiny fragment is a minute piece.

clue.text: Recanter could be a coward

indicators.note: could be says the word before can be turned into something else, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who retracts their beliefs might be thought cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word means a craven, disloyal person, a faint-hearted deserter.

clue.text: Tolerable and therefore repeatable

indicators.note: repeatable invites the solver to say the word twice in a row

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: Something passable is worth hearing again.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or mediocre means only passable.

clue.text: Secret new believer not given name

indicators.note: not given means left out, so the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: a convert has newly adopted a faith

explanation.surface: A recent religious recruit keeps their name hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden or clandestine activity is covert.

clue.text: Number returning to pub in Herts town

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the number is read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A figure goes back to the local in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, a county north of London; BARNET was historically a town there, now a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipping Barnet was a Hertfordshire market town.

clue.text: Scandinavian from the north — 'Unter possibly

parts.note: a hunter is a kind of horse; written 'Unter with the H dropped, a horse likewise becomes 'orse

explanation.surface: A Norseman from the far north is perhaps out hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unter shows the dropped H of some accents; the same treatment of the horse it exemplifies gives ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the language of medieval Scandinavians, and the word describes them.

clue.text: A girl starts to beat lad energetically — charming!

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: A girl begins to thrash a boy with vigour, which is somehow delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovable or sweet is delightful.

clue.text: Weapon making oblique contact — not good

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: a glance is a blow that strikes at an angle

explanation.surface: A weapon strikes only a slanting blow, which is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is a weapon.

clue.text: Row in which ferocious beast loses heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a tiger is a ferocious beast

explanation.surface: A fierce animal in a line becomes dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' removes G, the central letter of TIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank or level, as in theatre seating, is a row.

clue.text: Handy religious building — that is getting any number accommodated

indicators.note: accommodated means housed, so the religious building takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: a convent houses nuns
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A conveniently located nunnery takes in any number of guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveniently placed or useful is handy.

clue.text: Offensive apprentice going around church

indicators.note: going around means surrounding, so the church's letters go inside

parts.note: to indent is an old verb meaning to bind an apprentice by indenture
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rude trainee wanders about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprentice' looks like a noun but is used as a verb: to bind someone by indentures.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or obscene behaviour is offensive.

clue.text: Man catches a gee-gee to be given label

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so the man's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
GG is a childish word for a horse, written as two letters

explanation.surface: A man grabs a horse and it gets labelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Labelled items have had a ticket attached.
